content.intro: Learn real-time features with django through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Real-Time Features with Django matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines real-time features with django as part of advanced ecosystem and specialized applications. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Polling and long-lived requests; WebSocket concepts; ASGI integration; Event-driven architectures; When to use a separate real-time service. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Polling and long-lived requests
items.text: Polling and long-lived requests is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: WebSocket concepts
items.text: For WebSocket concepts, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: ASGI integration
items.text: ASGI supports asynchronous request handling and protocol extensions, but application dependencies must also be compatible. Async configuration alone does not make blocking calls non-blocking.

items.title: Event-driven architectures
items.text: For Event-driven architectures, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: When to use a separate real-time service
items.text: When to use a separate real-time service crosses an application boundary. Define the data contract, timeouts/failure behavior, authorization and retry/idempotency rules; verify with synthetic input and avoid live secrets in practice.

content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to Polling and long-lived requests. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
